estesis:
SKILLS

estesis-backend-fastapi-vc-conventions
Layer: per-stack conventions reference
Gist: Authoritative §A–§S ruleset for writing VocalClub Python/FastAPI code — layers, naming, DI, errors, schemas, models, migrations, tests; stable section letters cited by the reviewer.

estesis-backend-fastapi-vc-code-review
Layer: per-stack reviewer
Gist: Pedantic 3-phase reviewer for VocalClub Python/FastAPI PRs; reads the conventions skill and the shared review-standards first, then adds a requirements gate (spec vs. tracker), a conventions pass (cites [conv: §X]), and design-quality checks in §T–§AB.

estesis-process-review-standards
Layer: shared review foundation
Gist: Single source of truth for how every Estesis reviewer behaves — severity buckets (one axis: 🔴🟠🟡🔵), continuous-numbered output format, verdict rules (APPROVE / REQUEST CHANGES / BLOCK), scope discipline, read-only default, noise filter; never triggered for actual reviews.

estesis-process-review-feedback
Layer: process / learning loop
Gist: Closes the feedback cycle for any reviewer skill — captures human edits/MR remarks into a normalized corrections journal, then promotes repeated patterns (rule of three) into SKILL.md patches for the target reviewer.

estesis-process-deep-brainstorm
Layer: process / pre-execution gate
Gist: Multi-wave Socratic analysis harness aligned to GSD stages; runs closed-choice decision gates, rich trade-off analysis, and produces a decision pack before implementation begins.

estesis-process-deep-research
Layer: process / research harness
Gist: Accuracy-first research workflow that fans out cheap sub-agents for search/fetch, adds quote-provenance and cross-source corroboration layers absent from the native deep-research, and reserves a strong model only for final adjudication and synthesis.

---

LAYERING PATTERN

The family uses a strict three-tier naming convention encoded directly in the skill slug: `{project}-{domain}-{stack}-{role}`. The first segment (`estesis`) is the project/org namespace. The second segment (`backend`, `process`) is the domain — whether the skill is tied to a runtime stack or to a cross-cutting workflow. The third segment, when present (`fastapi`, `csharp`, `react`, `swagger-spec`), identifies the specific technology stack, keeping stack knowledge out of the shared layers. The final segment names the role: `conventions` for the authoritative ruleset, `code-review` for the reviewer that enforces it, and `review-standards` for the foundation both depend on.

The shared-standards skill (`estesis-process-review-standards`) knows nothing about any stack; it owns only the review contract — severity scale, output format, verdict rules, and scope discipline. Every per-stack reviewer hard-requires it and reads it first, meaning the output format is always identical regardless of language or review type. The per-stack conventions skill (`estesis-backend-fastapi-vc-conventions`) is a pure reference — it has no procedural logic; it just owns stable-lettered rules. The per-stack reviewer then sits above both, reading conventions + standards and adding only what is stack-specific: the spec/tracker requirements gate and the design-quality checks (§T–§AB) reserved in the conventions skill's letter namespace. This makes the reviewer thin — most of its content is delegation.

The feedback skill (`estesis-process-review-feedback`) is a second-order process tool: it does not review code at all; it improves the reviewers by routing corrections back to exactly the right skill (or to the shared standards if the signal is general). The rule-of-three threshold and the two-stage capture/promote split prevent single-data-point noise from polluting the ruleset prematurely.

The SolidStats family (`solidstats-process-project-standards`, `solidstats-process-ts-standards`) borrowed the `{project}-{domain}-{role}` naming structure directly — using `solidstats` as the namespace and `process` as the domain for cross-cutting standards. It also adopted the pattern of separating a shared baseline (project-standards) from a stack-specific layer (ts-standards), mirroring how `estesis-process-review-standards` underpins the stack-specific reviewers. What SolidStats does not yet have (compared to the mature estesis family) is the reviewer tier itself, the feedback/learning loop, and the explicit §-lettered citation contract between conventions and reviewer skills.
